tier_rationale: A PoE camera exposing standard ONVIF and RTSP, recordable to a microSD card or any NVR the owner runs, with person and vehicle detection performed on the camera and no subscription. Reolink does operate a cloud and an app, so this is D2 rather than D1 — but the local-only deployment is fully supported rather than a workaround.
the_unplug_test: It keeps recording and you keep watching. Point it at your own recorder over RTSP — Blue Iris, Frigate, Synology Surveillance Station, ZoneMinder, or Reolink's own NVR — and the footage lands on hardware in your house. Person and vehicle detection runs on the camera itself, so it works with the WAN blocked and costs nothing per month. What you lose without internet is remote viewing from outside the house, push notifications to the phone app, and firmware downloads. Note one real catch: the smart-detection events are exposed through Reolink's own software, not through ONVIF, so a third-party NVR sees the video but not necessarily the detections.
offline_losses: remote viewing from outside the local network
push notifications to the Reolink phone app

repairability.notes: PoE over a single Ethernet run means no power brick and no battery to age out — the most repairable thing about it is that the cable is standard.

sources.supports: Independent analysis establishing that smart person/vehicle detection runs locally on the camera rather than in the cloud, with no subscription required. Also records the limitation that these detections are exposed through Reolink's own software and NVR rather than through the ONVIF standard.

Independent review confirming ONVIF and RTSP support and integration with third-party NVR systems including Blue Iris, Frigate, Synology Surveillance Station and ZoneMinder, and recording to microSD or NVR without cloud.

open_questions: Does the camera contact Reolink servers by default when it has internet, and can that be disabled in the camera's own settings rather than at the firewall? Neither source establishes this and it is the main thing separating this record from a confident D2.
Can firmware updates be declined? Unresolved.

Confirm from Reolink's own documentation — rather than third-party reviews — that RTSP and ONVIF are enabled without any account. Both current sources are Class B; a first-party source would strengthen this record.

notes: Listed because the Security & Access domain page recommends ONVIF cameras with a recorder you own, and a recommendation with no example behind it is not worth much. This record also forced a correction to the ladder: D1's original wording would have allowed 'block it at the firewall' to promote almost anything, so D1 now requires that the vendor operate no cloud for the device at all.
local_replacement_note: RTSP and ONVIF feed straight into Frigate, Blue Iris, Synology Surveillance Station or ZoneMinder on your own hardware. One caveat: Reolink's on-camera person/vehicle detections are exposed through Reolink's own software rather than ONVIF, so a third-party recorder sees the video but may not see the detections.
